Inefficiencies (cost, then fix):
- I1 [substantiated] Stop-hook nudges from an external hook (~/.claude/stop-hook-git-check.sh, outside the repo). At least five "uncommitted changes… commit and push" nudges (19:26:23 uuid 4e799a19; 19:54:32 a097fc6c; 19:55:48 7633bae6; 19:57:56 02ca5d6e) plus "Unverified" nudges (11:58:57; 21:59:57 uuid b83fe262). Each drew a refusal turn, about 7 extra turns. Fix: the hook skips while `holyagent status` shows Running Assignments and accepts the holyagent identity rule, which it currently contradicts.
- I2 [substantiated] Destructive step approved before diagnosis. The user approved deleting artifacts (page 944283), then Worker.operations (wf_35ae34de) ran and found 0 artifacts with an account/org quota (TaskUpdate 13:12:58, uuid c2e576b1). Cost: one question, one workflow, no effect. Fix: holyagent.md:128 already requires reading the failure message first; extend it to check the target before asking for approval.
- I3 [substantiated] Report recovery. 10:34:26 (uuid 2a23a616) Bash python reads workflow journal.jsonl and writes r-*.txt into the scratchpad, because Workflow results came back cached or empty. Repeated for each close (`assignment close … < $S/r-….txt`). Cost: 2+ Bash calls per Assignment. Fix: `assignment close --workflow <runId> --agent <key>` reads the journal, or Workflow returns keyed reports inline.
- I4 [substantiated] Acceptance rejected, page 1136037 (19:51–19:54): `error: InsufficientAcceptance: … report's evidence: block has no support for criterion …`, plus `error: InvalidPath`. Cost: retries and re-closes. Fix: `assignment close --dry-run` lists criteria lacking support and names them in the hint.
- I5 [substantiated] Identity question blocked the push for about 12.5 h (22:00:02 to 10:34:20). holyagent.md:146 says to proceed on the recommended default when the user does not answer. Fix: record the default in the Intent and push the non-identity work.
- I6 [inference] Rework. Worker.implementation wf_66760a86 launched 19:55:32; TaskCreate at 19:55:40 says it "será em parte substituída pela migração" after the user's TanStack question (19:54:59). At least part of one writer-and-review cycle was redone (m1–m3, bca31dd). Fix: when a user question may change scope, plan and ask before dispatching writers.
- I7 [unverified] Per-result total_cost_usd values (9–70) do not reconcile with get_session cost_usd 49.54. Use one counter in the report.

Intent state (.holyagent):
- S1 [substantiated] Intent entregar-o-eureka-0-1-0-como-prs-intent-0mv9ynm3f-6zpg, rev 47, is committed on origin/release/v0.1.0/version (9fdeaeee, 2026-10-26 11:57:54, author David). Revs 41–46 are on the same branch. PR #29's head, release/v0.1.0/ship-vite, has the code but not this state. The root noticed the split at 18:49.
- S2 [substantiated] 18:49:47 (uuid 67c350fc): the root ran `git switch -c release/v0.1.0/ship-vite --track …` in the main checkout and `git worktree add /home/user/wt/version -b release/v0.1.0/version …` for state. Two stack branches are now checked out side by side.
- S3 [substantiated] Every `vcs commit` ran as `cd /home/user/wt/version && H=… vcs commit`. Commits (e5bcc0f, f0723a1c, b3b3134b and later) landed on ship-vite, per the stop-hook text and the reflog. docs/commit-authorship.md:18 says a linked worktree with no Intent in use stages its whole .holyagent/intents folder with the commit.
- S4 [inference, unverified] Intent state may have ridden the ship-vite commits, duplicating or splitting it from the rev-47 lineage on version. No event shows .holyagent paths in a commit. Confirm with `git log --stat` on both branches.
- S5 [substantiated] No checkout block, lost state or state conflict appears in the events. The only unexplained refusal is `InvalidPath` (page 1136037).
- S6 [substantiated] holyagent.md Stack plan (112–121) and Version control (98–110) do not say which branch holds a stack's Intent state, so the root had no rule to apply. Proposal for the user's point: one state home per Intent (the base-most stack branch or a named state branch); `vcs commit` refuses Intent state from a worktree whose branch is not that home; the Stack plan names the home.
